It landed directly on main rather than on a dedicated fork/patches branch, which is a documented deviation from the tier 2 procedure in fork/README.md section 4, not a template for future patches.

adaptations.summary: Underlagsjakt extension: the surface where Mattias answers bertil's underlagsjakt questions (bertil contract 1.1), enabled through extensions.config.json and upstream's generated extension registry. Includes the extension's own machine path (lib/leverans.ts), so bertil can deliver the export and collect answers without a browser session, gated by UNDERLAGSJAKT_LEVERANS_TOKEN and UNDERLAGSJAKT_LEVERANS_ORGNR on the box.
adaptations.why: Mattias decision 2026-09-17: the answers belong in this backoffice, built as an extension rather than in core so every upstream catch-up stays mergeable. The code is wholly new files under extensions/general/underlagsjakt/ and components/extensions/general/. Enabling it goes through the sanctioned extension seam, which unavoidably touches upstream-owned files: extensions.config.json (one id appended), the committed registry under lib/extensions/_generated/ (regenerated by npm run setup:extensions, additive lines only), lib/extensions/__tests__/sectors.test.ts, which pins the number of enabled extensions and fails otherwise, and messages/sv.json plus messages/en.json, where i18n/__tests__/message-keys.test.ts requires every UI string to live (one new top-level `underlagsjakt` namespace, inserted mid-file before `extensions` so upstream's usual appends at the end do not touch the same lines). On an upstream merge that touches these files, keep upstream's lines, re-append the id, rerun setup:extensions and recount.

adaptations.summary: docker-publish.yml publishes to ghcr.io/tyrberg/accounted instead of upstream's ghcr.io/erp-mafia/gnubok.
adaptations.why: Upstream's GHCR namespace is scoped to the erp-mafia GitHub App installation, which this fork does not have. Every push to main since 2026-09-05 has failed both platform builds identically at the push-by-digest step, before either platform reaches the merge job (runs 35246610958 on 2026-09-17, 33984840175 and 33955376313 on 2026-09-05): 'ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: failed to push ghcr.io/erp-mafia/gnubok: denied: permission_denied: The requested installation does not exist.' The fork can only push under a namespace it owns, so IMAGE_NAME moves to tyrberg/accounted: it matches this fork's actual GitHub repo, Tyrberg/accounted, rather than the old gnubok codename upstream still uses for the image itself. Every other reference in this workflow (metadata extraction, the push-by-digest outputs line, the per-arch buildcache cache-from/cache-to tags, the sentinel-verification digest lookup, the merge job's tag list, imagetools create/inspect, cosign sign, the Trivy image-ref) resolves through the IMAGE_NAME env var, either as the workflow expression env.IMAGE_NAME or as the shell variable of the same name, so the one env line is the whole fix; confirmed by grep that no other line in this file hardcodes erp-mafia/gnubok. It modifies an upstream-owned file (.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml), so it is a genuine tier 2 patch. Like docker-cron-entrypoint-hardening it lands directly on main rather than on a dedicated fork/patches branch: a repeat of the same documented deviation from the fork/README.md section 4 procedure, because standing up a whole patch-series branch for a one-line env value is out of proportion. This will never go upstream (upstream's own namespace is correct for upstream), so upstream.status is not-applicable rather than planned.

checks.reason: The image namespace no longer reads tyrberg/accounted, so a push either targets upstream's namespace again (denied: permission_denied: The requested installation does not exist) or some other value nothing here has verified.
Upstream's namespace reappeared somewhere in this file, which means a future push will fail the same installation-does-not-exist error this adaptation exists to fix.

adaptations.summary: docker-publish.yml only moves the latest tag from a run whose commit is still the tip of main.
adaptations.why: Upstream tags latest unconditionally on every main build (type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}), and two runs started by merges in quick succession have no ordering, so whichever pushes last wins. On 2026-09-21 PR #15 (b6f644653) and PR #16 (cb596981a) built two seconds apart, both succeeded, and latest ended up on b6f644653: a pull of latest silently deployed an app without #16. The merge job now reads the tip of the default branch with git ls-remote (the repo is public, so no token or permission change is needed) and enables latest only when it equals GITHUB_SHA; a superseded run keeps its sha tag, which is the rescue path that deployed cb596981a correctly. A concurrency group was not used: it cancels pending runs, which would drop their sha tags, and it serializes runs without ordering them by commit. Operator dispensation 2026-09-21 (task 1480) covers this tagging step only. upstream.status is not-applicable: upstream has not asked for it, and the fix stands on its own here.

checks.reason: latest is no longer gated on the tip check, so two merges in quick succession can leave it pointing at the older commit again.
The step that compares this run's commit with the tip of main is gone or changed, so the latest gate no longer means what it claims.
The immutable sha tag is gone. It is the rescue path when latest is skipped, and the only way a superseded build stays deployable.

adaptations.summary: docker/extensions.self-hosted.json lists underlagsjakt, so the published image actually contains the extension.
adaptations.why: The Dockerfile copies docker/extensions.<preset>.json over the repo-root extensions.config.json and then runs setup:extensions, so the registration that underlagsjakt-extension makes in extensions.config.json is discarded at image build time. Without this line the extension is in the source tree and green in the fork's tests, but absent from every image we publish: on the first deploy of our own image on 2026-09-17 the operator found no Underlagsjakt entry in the UI, and the running container had no extensions.config.json containing it. upstream.status is not-applicable: the preset is upstream's list of the extensions it ships, and this one is ours.

checks.reason: The image build reads this preset, not extensions.config.json. If underlagsjakt falls out of it the extension silently disappears from the deployed app while every other check stays green.

adaptations.summary: api-mfa-gate.ts listar underlagsjaktens leveransvag bland de sokvagar vars auth-kontrakt ar Authorization-rubriken.
adaptations.why: Underlagsjaktens export- och svarsrutter ar en maskinvag: bertil postar utan att en manniska ar inloggad. Rutterna deklarerar skipAuth och autentiserar sjalva via authenticateLeverans, som binder bolaget till UNDERLAGSJAKT_LEVERANS_ORGNR och jamfor token i konstant tid mot en nyckel som maste vara minst 32 tecken. Men MFA-grinden i lib/supabase/middleware.ts kor FORE dispatchern och avvisade anropet med 401, eftersom BEARER_AUTH_PREFIXES bara listade /api/v1/ och mcp-serverns rutt. Upptackt vid forsta skarpa leveransforsoket 2026-09-20: bade med och utan nyckel gav 401, och ingenting nadde extensionen. Prefixet galler endast underlagsjaktens egna rutter och slapper inte igenom nagot annat, och grinden kraver fortfarande att Authorization-rubriken finns.

checks.reason: Faller prefixet bort slutar bertils leverans fungera med 401 fran middleware, utan att nagot i extensionen sager ifran.
